One news app. Start reading Medical Daily Joseph James National Norovirus Levels Sit Low but Florida Is Entering the Months When Stomach Bug Outbreaks Usually Climb Norovirus Florida CDC Norovirus, the leading cause of vomiting and diarrhea in the United States, is circulating at low levels nationally as fall begins, according to the most recent federal and academic surveillance data. For Florida, which has ranked among the states with the most confirmed outbreaks, that quiet stretch is unlikely to last through the coming months. The CDC's NoroSTAT outbreak tracker, updated Sept. 17, counted 27 outbreaks from Aug. 1 through Sept. 4 in its participating states, compared with 29 during the same period last year. That is within the normal range for this point in the season. Florida is not one of the states that report to NoroSTAT, so the tracker does not reflect conditions there. The reason to pay attention now is timing. Norovirus activity typically rises in the fall and peaks in winter. With schools in session, long-term care facilities heading into respiratory virus season, and Florida's winter cruise season approaching, the next few weeks are a practical window for families to prepare. A Quiet Start in the Latest Surveillance Numbers Wastewater testing offers the broadest early signal. In its latest nationwide wastewater monitoring update, published in early September, the WastewaterSCAN program, run by Stanford University and Emory University, reported that norovirus was detected in every sample it analyzed in August. Even so, median concentrations fell about 12% from July, and the program placed norovirus in its low category nationally with no clear trend over the prior three weeks. Its Southern region includes Florida, though the update did not break out Florida sites. That is likely to change. In the 2024 to 2025 season, WastewaterSCAN saw norovirus levels start rising in early October and peak in early February. How high each winter peak climbs can vary from year to year. These numbers have limits. Norovirus is not individually reportable to the CDC, most clinics do not test for it, and outbreak data arrive weeks after illnesses occur. The figures describe direction, not how many people in any Florida county are sick right now. Florida's Track Record and Crowded Settings Florida has ranked near the top for confirmed outbreaks. Between Sept. 1, 2023, and Oct. 31, 2024, the state reported 24 confirmed norovirus outbreaks, second only to California, according to CDC data reported by CBS News Miami. Cruise ships were hit hard that year, with 16 outbreaks reported in 2024, five of them in December. Local signals can also differ from state trends. Last January, WUSF reported that Florida's wastewater levels were mostly steady statewide while Orange County saw a noticeable rise, a reminder that Orlando, Miami, Tampa and Jacksonville can move on different timelines. Nationally, the CDC estimates norovirus causes 19 million to 21 million illnesses each year, according to its norovirus facts and statistics. The agency's outbreak overview says about 2,500 outbreaks are reported annually, and roughly half of all foodborne disease outbreaks are caused by norovirus, often when an infected food worker handles ready-to-eat food. The virus spreads through tiny particles of vomit or stool, and people can shed it for two weeks or more after they feel better. Nursing homes, schools, child care centers, and cruise ships are among the places it spreads fastest. Dehydration Signs, Home Care and When to Get Help Symptoms usually start 12 to 48 hours after exposure and include sudden vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, and stomach cramps, sometimes with fever, headache, or body aches. Most healthy people recover in one to three days. The main danger is dehydration. Young children account for many emergency visits, while most of the roughly 900 norovirus deaths each year in the United States occur in adults 65 and older, according to the CDC. Warning signs include urinating much less, a dry mouth and throat, and dizziness when standing. In children, crying with few or no tears and unusual sleepiness or fussiness are red flags. Severe dehydration may require IV fluids and needs prompt medical care. Handwashing is the main defense, since no vaccine or specific antiviral treatment is available. "Like all viruses, the biggest thing is hand-washing," Dr. Carlos Abanses, medical director of the pediatric emergency department at St. Joseph's Children's Hospital in Tampa, told WUSF. Soap and water work better than alcohol-based hand sanitizer alone against this virus, a practical point for classrooms and cruise cabins alike. Families can also clean contaminated hard surfaces with a chlorine bleach solution, wash soiled laundry on the longest cycle at the hottest setting, and keep sick people from preparing food for others until at least two days after symptoms stop. Oral rehydration solutions can help with mild dehydration, and antibiotics do not work against norovirus. Residents without a regular doctor can contact their county health department or a community health center. MedicalDaily will report when the seasonal rise begins or if Florida officials issue local warnings. There is no sign of a norovirus surge in current national data, but Florida is entering the months when outbreaks usually build, and older adults and young children carry the highest risk when they do. Key Questions Answered Is norovirus rising in Florida right now? Current national data show low levels, and the latest wastewater update found no clear upward trend. NoroSTAT does not include Florida, so local data are limited. When does norovirus season usually start? Activity typically climbs in fall and peaks in winter. In the 2024 to 2025 season, wastewater levels began rising in early October and peaked in early February. Who is most at risk? Young children, adults 65 and older, and people with weakened immune systems face the greatest risk of dehydration. Does hand sanitizer work? Not well on its own. Washing with soap and water is more effective against norovirus. When should someone seek medical care? For signs of dehydration such as little urination, dizziness when standing, or a child crying without tears or being unusually sleepy. How long are people contagious? People can spread the virus while sick and for two weeks or more after they feel better. Sign up to read this article Read news from 100's of titles, curated specifically for you. Warning signs include urinating much less, a dry mouth and throat, and dizziness when standing. In children, crying with few or no tears and unusual sleepiness or fussiness are red flags. Severe dehydration may require IV fluids and needs prompt medical care. Handwashing is the main defense, since no vaccine or specific antiviral treatment is available. "Like all viruses, the biggest thing is hand-washing," Dr. Carlos Abanses, medical director of the pediatric emergency department at St. Joseph's Children's Hospital in Tampa, told WUSF. Soap and water work better than alcohol-based hand sanitizer alone against this virus, a practical point for classrooms and cruise cabins alike. Families can also clean contaminated hard surfaces with a chlorine bleach solution, wash soiled laundry on the longest cycle at the hottest setting, and keep sick people from preparing food for others until at least two days after symptoms stop. Oral rehydration solutions can help with mild dehydration, and antibiotics do not work against norovirus. Residents without a regular doctor can contact their county health department or a community health center. MedicalDaily will report when the seasonal rise begins or if Florida officials issue local warnings. There is no sign of a norovirus surge in current national data, but Florida is entering the months when outbreaks usually build, and older adults and young children carry the highest risk when they do. Key Questions Answered Is norovirus rising in Florida right now? Current national data show low levels, and the latest wastewater update found no clear upward trend. NoroSTAT does not include Florida, so local data are limited. When does norovirus season usually start? Activity typically climbs in fall and peaks in winter. In the 2024 to 2025 season, wastewater levels began rising in early October and peaked in early February. Who is most at risk? Young children, adults 65 and older, and people with weakened immune systems face the greatest risk of dehydration. Does hand sanitizer work? Not well on its own. Washing with soap and water is more effective against norovirus. When should someone seek medical care? For signs of dehydration such as little urination, dizziness when standing, or a child crying without tears or being unusually sleepy. How long are people contagious? People can spread the virus while sick and for two weeks or more after they feel better. Sign up to read this article Read news from 100's of titles, curated specifically for you. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily PharmaVoice newsletter. Some of the biggest news and trends captured in PharmaVoice's newsletter this week. Sign up here to receive the newsletter daily. A norovirus vaccine breakthrough? Norovirus has long evaded effective drug development, partly due to the compact structure of its genome. Now, researchers at Yale University may have discovered a way to untangle the virus' RNA. In the study, scientists disrupted parts of the virus' folded RNA structure, causing them to "unzip." The research was effective in mouse models and could have broader implications for other RNA viruses like influenza, the scientists reported. They're not the only researchers looking to outwit norovirus. This week, we featured a conversation with the new CEO of Cocrystal Pharma on the biotech's antiviral norovirus candidate and why it might succeed as a treatment where vaccines have traditionally failed in prevention. Evvy pulls in $40 million for its healthtech platform for women Innovative approaches to tackling women's health are still stoking excitement among some investors. Evvy, a company that developed a vaginal microbiome test, just pulled in $40 million as part of a series B fundraising haul. Evvy said 100,000 patients have used its platform, which can diagnose fertility issues while offering personalized treatments and biomarker tracking. The funding will help Evvy validate new AI-powered diagnostic and care models. As more companies try to unravel women's health issues, boosting female participation in drug trials remains a critical piece of the puzzle — an ongoing issue we looked at this week. Sling's fundraising fling Sling Therapeutics' $123 million financing announced Wednesday came with a clear next step: a phase 3 trial. The biotech raised the money to advance its experimental pill for thyroid eye disease and announced that the first patients have been dosed in its confirmatory study. Sling is banking on the competitive advantage of an oral treatment over the disease's approved injectable therapies. That's a venture financing tale. But it puts a familiar question in focus for companies approaching the public markets: What will the next round of money accomplish? For the eight biotech IPO prospects we examined this week, the answers vary. Some are seeking funding for pivotal trials. Others still need more capital to complete future studies. Their clinical evidence, financing needs and readiness for public ownership make for very different investment propositions. news.content_title: Norovirus suspected in Tbilisi kindergarten outbreak – over 100 hospitalized
news.content: (Interpressnews.) TBILISI, September 20 – Georgian health officials say norovirus was most likely responsible for a massive outbreak of stomach illness at public kindergartens in Tbilisi, with more than 100 children hospitalized. Most of the children are now recovering, but investigators have yet to establish how the infection spread. The National Center for Disease Control said Sunday that laboratory results pointed to norovirus as the likely cause of the great majority of cases. It stressed that testing was continuing and that no child had suffered serious or dangerous complications. The outbreak began on Thursday, with children developing symptoms including vomiting, abdominal pain and fever. By Friday, authorities had reported illness among 55 children and one staff member at 20 kindergartens, and seven facilities had suspended activities. On Saturday, Health Minister Mikheil Sarjveladze said more than 100 children had required hospitalization, although none was considered at risk of serious complications. Hospitals reported further improvement on Sunday. Eight children remained at Iashvili Children’s Central Hospital after six were discharged that day. Their conditions were stable. Another six children were receiving treatment at Tsitsishvili Children’s New Clinic, where six others were considered well enough to be discharged. Despite norovirus now confirmed as the likely infectious agent behind the outbreak, it is still unclear how the virus spread to the children. Infectious disease specialist Maia Butsashvili said Sunday that the appearance of cases at 20 kindergartens at about the same time strongly suggested contaminated food. She called for urgent checks of food supplies and people involved in preparing and distributing meals. The health authorities have not identified a particular food product as the source. On Saturday, Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze urged the public not to assume that food was responsible or rule it out before the investigation was complete. He said kindergarten suppliers must provide laboratory test reports for their products and promised action if the inquiry found mistakes by city authorities. The Health Ministry said the state would cover the children’s medical bills and that parents should not be charged for treatment related to the outbreak

news.content_zh: (Interpressnews)第比利斯,9月20日 - 根据格鲁吉亚卫生官员的说法,诺如病毒最可能引发了第比利斯公立幼儿园中大规模的急性胃肠炎暴发,超过100名儿童住院治疗。大多数儿童目前正在恢复,但调查人员尚未确定感染是如何传播的。国家疾病控制中心周日表示,实验室结果指向诺如病毒是大多数病例的可能原因。该中心强调,检测工作仍在继续,且没有儿童出现严重或危险的并发症。暴发始于周四,儿童出现呕吐、腹痛和发烧等症状。到周五,当局报告称在20所幼儿园中有55名儿童和一名工作人员患病,且有七所设施已暂停运营。周六,卫生部长米凯尔·萨尔日瓦拉泽表示,超过100名儿童需要住院治疗,尽管没有一人被认为有严重并发症的风险。

news.content: bpn.ge 22 Sep 23 Sep USD 2.6074 2.6104 EUR 2.9941 2.9933 RUB 3.1022 3.1028 Eng Geo Rus Tue / 22 Sep / 2026 23:53:13 Home Politics Economics Region Military Matters Culture Society Conflicts Justice World Sport Other Announcements Interview Opinion Politics 20.09.2026 / 10:59 a a According to the National Center for Disease Control, laboratory test results indicate that norovirus was highly likely to be the causative agent in the vast majority of gastroenteritis cases reported in kindergartens According to the National Center for Disease Control, laboratory test results indicate that norovirus was highly likely to have been the cause of the vast majority of gastroenteritis cases reported in kindergartens. According to the Center, this pathogen is the leading cause of viral gastroenteritis worldwide. Based on data from Georgia, norovirus is responsible for 40-45% of viral gastroenteritis cases. “Immediately after cases of gastroenteritis were identified among children attending kindergartens on September 17, the National Center for Disease Control and Public Health became involved in the investigation within the scope of its competence. First and foremost, it should be noted that, at this stage, the clinical course of the cases is favorable. None of the cases has resulted in significant or dangerous complications, and the majority of the children are already in the recovery phase and will soon return to their normal routines. Laboratory test results related to the illness indicate that norovirus was highly likely to have been the cause of the vast majority of cases. It should also be noted that the investigations are ongoing, and the public will be informed as soon as the final results are available. This pathogen is the leading cause of viral gastroenteritis worldwide. According to data from Georgia, norovirus is responsible for 40-45% of viral gastroenteritis cases. Norovirus is an infection characterized by vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea and, in some cases, fever. It is not life-threatening, and the body generally overcomes the infection on its own within 1-3 days. Treatment involves maintaining the body’s fluid and electrolyte balance. During norovirus infection, it is important to ensure proper hydration and restore lost fluids; follow an appropriate diet by avoiding dairy products, fatty, fried and spicy foods for at least 3-4 days; and take medications for diarrhea and vomiting only as prescribed by a doctor. In addition, maintaining proper hygiene is important for preventing the spread of norovirus - hands should be washed with soap for at least 20 seconds, and contaminated surfaces should be properly disinfected. It should also be noted that, from the very first stage, the relevant services of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture became involved in investigating food safety at childcare and educational institutions,” the statement reads. v-if="article.gallery" v-html="article.gallery" Tweet (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); news.content: "Hearst Magazines and Yahoo may earn commission or revenue on some items through these links." You've heard all about "Brat Summer" but do you know about the B.R.A.T. diet? This food plan is the complete opposite of the brat party girl vibe, but it is the secret to calming all kinds of tummy issues. This clinical diet plan — which stands for b ananas, r ice, a pplesauce and t oast — is what registered dietitians use when patients have acute diarrhea, nausea or certain kinds of stomach bugs, like norovirus . That's because these foods are mild, easily digested and a good way of getting some nutrients without irritating your stomach further. "For some people, eating makes things feel better, and for others that's not so," says Tamara Duker Freuman , M.S., R.D., C.D.N., author of The Bloated Belly Whisperer: See Results Within a Week and Tame Digestive Distress Once and for All . Overall, nibbling something bland and non-acidic like toast or oatmeal can be soothing if you have indigestion or a queasy stomach. "An empty stomach can definitely worsen nausea," says nutritionist Joy Bauer , M.S., R.D.N., C.D.N., author of Joy Bauer's Superfood! . (Of course, if you suspect the cause of your G.I. problems isn't dietary, see a gastroenterologist to get to the root of the issue.) Here are 15 B.R.A.T. bites and beverages that could help calm an uneasy gut. We also noted some troublesome foods to avoid when you're feeling queasy. Kefir Photo credit: Antons Jevterevs / EyeEm - Getty Images "Kefir is a probiotic-rich, fermented milk drink that has a tart and tangy flavor, and a thin consistency," says Stefani Sassos, M.S., R.D.N., C.S.O., C.D.N., NASM-CPT , Good Housekeeping's resident dietitian. "It provides a healthy dose of diverse probiotics, which can help balance the gut microbiome. It's also been shown to support a healthy immune system and suppress viral infections." This may alleviate some discomfort and help you feel better. Look for varieties that are low in sugar, as options with higher sugar may exacerbate symptoms. Green beans Photo credit: Annie Otzen - Getty Images Raw vegetables can be difficult to digest, but plain boiled or steamed ones, like green beans, can be easier for your system to process, and they'll provide a dose of nutrients your body needs to function well and fight off what's plaguing you, Sassos says. Applesauce Photo credit: Brycia James - Getty Images Applesauce is an awesome aid to get your stomach back in working order," says Jessica Stamm , M.S., R.D.N., a registered dietitian nutritionist in California. It's easy to digest but still delivers important nutrients like pectin (a type of fiber) and potassium, a mineral that functions as an electrolyte to help keep fluid levels balanced. Carrots Photo credit: boblin - Getty Images Cooked carrots are a great way to boost nutrition and flavor when your menu is limited. "Cooking vegetables like carrots or spinach makes them easier to digest, and they're perfect in egg scrambles or broth-based soups," Stamm says. RELATED: Easy, Comforting Soup Recipes to Make White rice Photo credit: Roberto Machado Noa - Getty Images "You may be tempted to go for whole grain, high fiber options when it comes to carbs, but gentle is best when your tummy is uneasy," Stamm says. Because white rice is low in fiber, it's easier to digest, and bland enough to soothe an upset stomach. Chicken Photo credit: Kseniya Ovchinnikova - Getty Images Getting a bit of protein is important, even when you're feeling icky, but reach for things like chicken or fish, which are easier to digest and prepared plainly compared to fattier red meat. "Unseasoned proteins can be a good addition to your plain white rice or a baked sweet potato," Stamm says. Bananas Photo credit: Getty Images "Bananas are great because they're easy to digest and considered non-irritating for the stomach and upper gastrointestinal tract," says Julie Upton, M.S., R.D., co-founder of Appetite for Health . The high-fiber fruit not only keeps the system regular and aids in recovering from diarrhea, but the vitamin B6 also reduces bloating caused by fluid retention and the magnesium helps to relax muscles. White Toast Photo credit: littleny - Getty Images While it may seem counterintuitive, keeping your belly empty when feeling queasy can create more nausea because there's nothing in the system to absorb stomach acid. Upton suggests nibbling on white toast or soda crackers every few hours since the starches from these simple carbohydrates "lack fiber, protein and fat — all of which slow digestion and sit in your stomach longer." Eggs Photo credit: Getty Images "High-fat sources of protein, like processed or red meats and fried food, can cause reflux — especially if you're consuming large amounts late at night," Jaclyn London , M.S., R.D., C.D.N., a registered dietitian and the author of Dressing on the Side (and Other Diet Myths Debunked) , says. "Eggs are an easier-to-digest alternative and an easy way to meet your protein needs without getting too full, too fast." Oats Photo credit: Synergee - Getty Images Adding whole grains can both soothe tummy ailments and prevent any future intestinal issues. "Soluble fiber from oats draws water into your digestive tract and moves food through your body," London says. Aim to hit at least 25 to 35 grams of total fiber per day, but don't overdo it. "Both hunger and overeating can make nausea, bloating, abdominal pain and gas even worse," she adds. Tomatoes Photo credit: Getty Images Prebiotic foods — including produce, whole grains, pulses, nuts and seeds — can help "fuel" friendly gut bacteria in your GI tract, London explains. By stimulating that microbiome, prebiotics boost intestinal immunity and prevent inflammation, diarrhea, and other GI problems, according to 2013 research by the Institute of Food Technologists . Stock up on tomatoes, chicory, onions, asparagus and wheat for the best benefits. RELATED: Best Prebiotic Foods Sweet Potatoes Photo credit: Getty Images Foods that are rich in calcium, magnesium and potassium also reduce belly bloat by balancing out sodium. Plus, that's not all these minerals are good for: Calcium is essential for smooth muscle contraction which moves food through your digestive tract, potassium regulates fluid balance and magnesium activates the body's enzymes that are needed to break down food. Ginger Photo credit: Getty Images "Ginger tea, ginger supplements, ginger lozenges — ginger has been shown in some studies to help alleviate nausea and vomiting," Upton says. "In fact, it is often recommended for morning sickness and for chemotherapy-induced nausea." For children's tummy upsets, it's wise to consult with a pediatrician first before introducing new remedies. Water Photo credit: Getty Images Dehydration frequently causes constipation, so sipping unsweetened beverages like tea, as well as flat or sparkling water can keep everything moving along. Most people need a minimum of eight cups per day. "Staying hydrated aids digestion and helps with gas and constipation," says Bauer. RELATED: How Much Water You Really Should Be Drinking Every Day Coffee Photo credit: Getty Images If you know your tummy troubles stem from constipation, London also recommends drinking a cup of joe first thing in the morning. Research has shown that caffeine plus coffee's plant-based antioxidants can help you stay regular. Avoid caffeinated beverages if you're sensitive, feeling nausea or have reflux unrelated to constipation. Coffee, however, is not a good idea for people for whom acid upsets their stomach, says Freuman. The Foods Not to Eat With an Upset Stomach: Photo credit: Hearst Owned Just as important as soothing a stomach issue is preventing it by knowing what not to eat. It's wise to steer clear of these common tummy triggers: Fried and greasy foods : "Fatty foods can be hard for the body to digest, and eating too much can cause diarrhea and bloating," says Bauer. Spicy foods: Hot, spicy food can trigger gastrointestinal distress such as reflux, indigestion and diarrhea for many people, Bauer says. Cruciferous veggies: "High-fiber veggies like broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, and cabbage are really good for you, but they can lead to gas, bloating, cramps, constipation, or diarrhea if you add too much into your diet too quickly," says Bauer. High-fiber foods: "Things like kale, beans, lentils, whole grains, and even popcorn are bulky, fibrous foods that take up a lot of space, and in general these are the most likely to provoke the G.I. system," Freuman says. Sugar and sweetener: Sweeteners, including natural sugars, can be troublesome for some people. "Sorbitol and xylitol, for example, can cause bloating, gas, or diarrhea," says Bauer. Alcoholic beverages: Alcohol can interfere with the secretion of gastric acid, and it relaxes the esophageal sphincter, allowing stomach acid to travel up the esophagus, causing indigestion. "It can also trigger diarrhea for some," says Bauer. You Might Also Like

Plus, that's not all these minerals are good for: Calcium is essential for smooth muscle contraction which moves food through your digestive tract, potassium regulates fluid balance and magnesium activates the body's enzymes that are needed to break down food. Ginger Photo credit: Getty Images "Ginger tea, ginger supplements, ginger lozenges — ginger has been shown in some studies to help alleviate nausea and vomiting," Upton says. "In fact, it is often recommended for morning sickness and for chemotherapy-induced nausea." For children's tummy upsets, it's wise to consult with a pediatrician first before introducing new remedies. Water Photo credit: Getty Images Dehydration frequently causes constipation, so sipping unsweetened beverages like tea, as well as flat or sparkling water can keep everything moving along. Most people need a minimum of eight cups per day. "Staying hydrated aids digestion and helps with gas and constipation," says Bauer. RELATED: How Much Water You Really Should Be Drinking Every Day Coffee Photo credit: Getty Images If you know your tummy troubles stem from constipation, London also recommends drinking a cup of joe first thing in the morning. Research has shown that caffeine plus coffee's plant-based antioxidants can help you stay regular. Avoid caffeinated beverages if you're sensitive, feeling nausea or have reflux unrelated to constipation. Coffee, however, is not a good idea for people for whom acid upsets their stomach, says Freuman. The Foods Not to Eat With an Upset Stomach: Photo credit: Hearst Owned Just as important as soothing a stomach issue is preventing it by knowing what not to eat. It's wise to steer clear of these common tummy triggers: Fried and greasy foods : "Fatty foods can be hard for the body to digest, and eating too much can cause diarrhea and bloating," says Bauer. Spicy foods: Hot, spicy food can trigger gastrointestinal distress such as reflux, indigestion and diarrhea for many people, Bauer says. Cruciferous veggies: "High-fiber veggies like broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, and cabbage are really good for you, but they can lead to gas, bloating, cramps, constipation, or diarrhea if you add too much into your diet too quickly," says Bauer. High-fiber foods: "Things like kale, beans, lentils, whole grains, and even popcorn are bulky, fibrous foods that take up a lot of space, and in general these are the most likely to provoke the G.I. system," Freuman says. Sugar and sweetener: Sweeteners, including natural sugars, can be troublesome for some people. "Sorbitol and xylitol, for example, can cause bloating, gas, or diarrhea," says Bauer. Alcoholic beverages: Alcohol can interfere with the secretion of gastric acid, and it relaxes the esophageal sphincter, allowing stomach acid to travel up the esophagus, causing indigestion. "It can also trigger diarrhea for some," says Bauer. You Might Also Like

news.content: WhatsApp Home Daily Culture Sport Media GIBRALTAR · 23 SEPT 2026 · 01:53| ☀️ 21,4°C · 3,0 m/s YesterdayPhotographic Society Competition Winners YesterdayGibraltar Sound Festival Returns Live to the Piazza This Saturday YesterdayGSD Proposes Changes To Residency Policy YesterdayLocal Man Sentenced To 14 Years For Child Sex Offences YesterdayTrinity Lighthouse Opens To The Public MonFinal Call For Heritage Awards 2026 MonSlipping Through My Fingers Play Opens This Week MonMichelle Roman Exhibition Opens Next Month - Interview YesterdayPhotographic Society Competition Winners YesterdayGibraltar Sound Festival Returns Live to the Piazza This Saturday YesterdayGSD Proposes Changes To Residency Policy YesterdayLocal Man Sentenced To 14 Years For Child Sex Offences YesterdayTrinity Lighthouse Opens To The Public MonFinal Call For Heritage Awards 2026 MonSlipping Through My Fingers Play Opens This Week MonMichelle Roman Exhibition Opens Next Month - Interview Daily GHA Issues Norovirus Advice By YGTV Newsroom5 months ago2 min read Public Health says it is aware of an increase in people in the community suffering from rapid onset diarrhoea and/or vomiting. The GHA is requesting that if you experience diarrhoea or vomiting, please do not go and visit your family or friends in hospital or ERS until 48 hours after your symptoms have stopped. A statement from the GHA follows below: Public Health are aware of an increase in people in the community suffering from rapid onset diarrhoea and/or vomiting. This is most likely due to norovirus, or the winter vomiting bug. This is typically a short-lived illness and although unpleasant, most people make a full recovery without needing medical care. The GHA is requesting that if you experience diarrhoea or vomiting, please do not go and visit your family or friends in hospital or ERS until 48 hours after your symptoms have stopped. If you are due to attend an outpatient appointment or radiology appointment such as breast screening and have had symptoms in the last 48 hours, please contact the relevant department, advise them that you are unwell and they will help to re-schedule your appointment. If you are concerned about your symptoms, please call 111 for advice. Director of Public Health, Dr Helen Carter, said: “Please do not visit your friends or family in hospital or ERS until 48 hours after your symptoms have stopped. The reason this is important is because norovirus is very infectious and you may pass the infection onto patients and staff. “The same advice applies to children returning to school. If they have had diarrhoea or vomiting, they should also remain at home until 48 hours after their symptoms have stopped, in order to help reduce further spread in the community. “Hand washing is essential to prevent the spread of this norovirus. Do not rely on using alcohol hand gels because these do not work for norovirus.”

news.content: Alasko Frozen Raspberries are being recalled in Canada for possible norovirus contamination. There is a norovirus outbreak that is associated with this product, but there is no separate notice about the outbreak yet, so we don’t know the patient age range, illness onset dates, or if anyone has been hospitalized. This information is on the recall page. The recalling firm is New Alasko L.P. These raspberries were sold at the retail level and to restaurants, hotels, and institutions in these provinces: Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, and Quebec. The recalled products include Alaska Frozen Raspberries, Whole, packaged in 1 kilogram plastic bags. There is a black heart on the package with the word “Alasko” inside it. The UPC number that is stamped on the product label is 6 95058 00205 4. The PO number is 138602 and the lot number is SY25314. The best if used by date is November 10, 2027. Also recalled is Alasko IQF (Individually Quick Frozen) Whole Raspberries. They are packaged in 5 kilogram lots of five packages that weigh 1 kilogram each. The UPC number for this item is 1 069505 800205 1. The lot number is SY25314, the PO number is 138602, and the best if used by date is November 10, 2027. If you purchased these raspberries, do not eat them and do not sell or serve them to others. You can throw them away in a secure trash can after first double bagging them so other people can’t see them, or you can contact your distributor to arrange for a refund, or return them to the store where you bought them. If you ate these raspberries, especially if they were eaten uncooked, monitor your health for the symptoms of norovirus for the next few days. If you do get sick, see your doctor. Most people do not need medical care, but some, especially the elderly, the very young, pregnant women, and people with chronic illnesses and compromised immune systems, may need care. The norovirus explanation has been questioned, and test results are pending. An investigation has been launched, and the scale of the incident remains under assessment.
news.content_zh: 正在对第比利斯幼儿园儿童集体患病事件进行初步调查,症状可能与中毒或病毒感染有关。诺如病毒解释受到质疑,检测结果尚未公布。已启动调查,事件规模仍在评估中。
news.summary_zh: 正在对第比利斯幼儿园儿童集体患病事件进行初步调查,症状可能与中毒或病毒感染有关。诺如病毒解释受到质疑,检测结果尚未公布。已启动调查,事件规模仍在评估中。

Here's why Rachel SchoutsenMorning Show Host & Journalist Published on Sep. 20, 2026, 11:36 AM Ever wonder why stomach bugs make the rounds during times of colder weather? Discover the science behind why gastrointestinal viruses such as the norovirus is more stable and transmissible in cooler, less humid conditions, and learn what you can do to stay healthy. Why do stomach bugs spike in the cooler months? As temperatures drop, cases of gastrointestinal viruses like norovirus increase.
